conversation:
Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today?
Patient: I'm 62 years old, male. I came in because I had some chest pain over the weekend, and I wanted to make sure everything was okay.
Doctor: Could you please provide your age, gender, and describe the chest pain you experienced over the weekend, including its location, duration, intensity, and any associated symptoms?
Patient: Sure. The chest pain was in my chest, and it lasted for about an hour. It wasn't too bad, but it was enough to make me worried. I didn't have any other symptoms with it, just some shortness of breath and it felt a little uncomfortable.
Doctor: Can you describe the exact location, radiation, and character of the chest pain? Also, were there any specific activities or triggers that preceded the pain?
Patient: The chest pain was in my chest, and it wasn't too bad, but it was enough to make me worried. It happened while I was doing yard work, and it was really hot over the weekend. I was short of breath and felt a little chest pain for about an hour. I didn't have any other symptoms with it, just some shortness of breath and it felt a little uncomfortable.
Doctor: Have you had any prior evaluations or tests for chest pain, such as an ECG, stress test, or cardiac enzymes?
Patient: No, I haven't had any prior evaluations or tests for chest pain like an ECG, stress test, or cardiac enzymes before this episode. I was pretty surprised because I didn't have any chest pain while doing my knee rehab exercises, so this was unexpected for me.
Doctor: Can you describe the exact location of the chest pain, whether it radiates to other areas, and what it feels like (e.g., pressure, sharp, burning)? Also, could you tell me more about the shortness of breath—when it started, how long it lasted, and if it was related to the chest pain?
Patient: The chest pain was in my chest, and it felt like pressure. It didn't radiate anywhere else. The shortness of breath started at the same time as the chest pain, and it lasted for about an hour. It was definitely related to the chest pain and made me really worried, especially because I didn't have any chest pain while doing my knee rehab exercises before.
Doctor: Could you please provide details about your current medications, any known allergies, and whether there is a family history of cardiovascular or respiratory conditions?
Patient: I don't take any medications right now, and I don't have any allergies. As for family history, there's no heart disease on my immediate family side, but there is some on my cousin's side.
Doctor: Could you please provide the results of any recent physical examination, including vital signs and findings from the cardiovascular and respiratory systems?
Patient: The doctor mentioned that they felt a little enlarged thyroid that wasn't tender, there was a carotid bruit on the right side, my lungs were clear, my heart had a regular rate and rhythm but with a three out of six systolic ejection murmur, my abdomen was soft, and there was a healed scar on my right knee from prior surgery with no lower extremity edema. They also said my blood pressure was still high when they checked it.
Doctor: Could you provide the exact blood pressure reading and the results of any cardiac enzyme tests, ECG, or imaging studies that have been performed?
Patient: I don't have the exact blood pressure reading, but they said it was still high when they checked it. As for the tests, the EKG was normal, and they did an echocardiogram which showed a little bit of low pumping function in my heart. They didn't mention any cardiac enzyme tests specifically, but I was told there were no blockages found in the ER.
Doctor: Could you provide the specific value of your blood pressure reading during the physical examination and the exact ejection fraction from the echocardiogram?
Patient: I don't have the exact blood pressure reading or the specific ejection fraction from the echocardiogram. I was told my blood pressure was still high when they checked it, and that there was a little bit of low pumping function in my heart, but they didn't give me the exact numbers.
Doctor: Could you please confirm if you were given any specific numbers for your blood pressure or ejection fraction during your examination? If not, could you let me know if there are any other details you might have about your heart function or blood pressure that you can share?
Patient: No, I wasn't given any specific numbers for my blood pressure or ejection fraction. The doctor just mentioned that my blood pressure was still high when they checked it and that there was a little bit of low pumping function in my heart. I don't have the exact details, but I know they're going to look into it further.
Doctor: Thank you for sharing that. I understand it can be concerning not having the exact numbers. Could you let me know if there were any other tests done related to your thyroid function or heart health during your ER visit?
Patient: No, I don't recall any other tests being done related to my thyroid function or heart health during my ER visit. They did mention an enlarged thyroid that wasn't tender, but they didn't run any specific tests on it. As for my heart, they did an EKG and an echocardiogram, but that's about it.
Doctor: Could you provide the exact value of your blood pressure and the specific ejection fraction percentage from the echocardiogram?
Patient: I don't have the exact value of my blood pressure or the specific ejection fraction percentage from the echocardiogram. The doctor mentioned my blood pressure was still high when they checked it, and there was a little bit of low pumping function in my heart, but they didn't give me the exact numbers.
Doctor: Could you please confirm if there were any other findings from your ER visit, such as thyroid function tests or additional cardiac evaluations?
Patient: No, I don't recall any other findings from my ER visit besides what was mentioned. They did note an enlarged thyroid that wasn't tender, but they didn't run any specific tests on it. As for my heart, they did an EKG and an echocardiogram, but that's about it. They didn't mention any other cardiac evaluations or thyroid function tests.
Doctor: Could you provide the exact blood pressure reading and the ejection fraction percentage from the echocardiogram?
Patient: I don't have the exact blood pressure reading or the specific ejection fraction percentage from the echocardiogram. The doctor mentioned my blood pressure was still high when they checked it, and there was a little bit of low pumping function in my heart, but they didn't give me the exact numbers.
Doctor: Thank you for sharing that. Could you please confirm if there were any other findings related to the enlarged thyroid or any other cardiac evaluations that were not previously mentioned?
Patient: No, I don't recall any other findings related to the enlarged thyroid or any other cardiac evaluations beyond what was already mentioned. They noted the thyroid was enlarged but not tender, and they did an EKG and echocardiogram for the heart. That's all I remember from the ER visit.

reference_so.subjective:
Basic information: 62-year-old male presenting with chest pain over the weekend

History of present illness: Chest pain lasting approximately one hour, with associated shortness of breath and discomfort. The chest pain occurred during yard work in hot weather. It was located in the chest, felt like pressure, and did not radiate. The shortness of breath started at the same time as the chest pain and lasted for about an hour. No other symptoms were reported apart from shortness of breath and discomfort.

Past history: No prior cardiac evaluations or tests for chest pain (e.g., ECG, stress test, cardiac enzymes). No history of cardiovascular conditions (hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, coronary artery disease). No medications or allergies. Family history of heart disease on cousin's side.
reference_so.objective:
Physical examination: Physical examination findings: Enlarged non-tender thyroid, right carotid bruit, clear lungs, regular heart rate and rhythm with a 3/6 systolic ejection murmur, soft abdomen, healed right knee scar, no lower extremity edema. Blood pressure was elevated.

Investigations: Auxiliary examination results: EKG was normal, echocardiogram showed low pumping function in the heart, no blockages found in the ER. Blood pressure was elevated but exact value not provided. Ejection fraction percentage not provided.
